title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: A debt-free balance sheet buys you survival in a downturn, but only working-capital velocity and capital turnover buy you high return on equity.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Desk

web_blocks.html: We reviewed ten years of Eimco Elecon's accounts using Screener, audited FY2015–FY2026 BSE/NSE filings, and CRISIL reports. That forensic sweep shows a sharp split in the business. The company pairs a fortress, near-zero-debt balance sheet with cyclical sales and chronically heavy working capital. While solvency has never been in doubt, turning accounting profits into free cash remains the main financial hurdle.

web_blocks.caption: Extended Audited Performance Bridge: FY24 → FY25 → FY26 → H1 FY27 (Standalone, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Profitability stepped up structurally after FY22, but ROE remains modest (8.6–12.0%) due to ~₹206 Cr of low-yield treasury liquidity and 219–335 day cash conversion cycles.

web_blocks.html: Three Forensic Red Flags & Mitigants: First, Other Income dependence stands out clearly in the P&L. From FY17 to FY26, treasury income of ₹9–17 Cr per year supplied 25–45% of Profit Before Tax, peaking at ₹17.05 Cr (33.9% of PBT) in FY26. Second, CFO-to-EBITDA conversion is lumpy across the cycle. Over FY15–FY24, total Operating Profit was ₹196 Cr while total CFO was ₹124 Cr (~63% conversion). In FY26, conversion slipped to ~51% (₹22.1 Cr CFO on ₹43.0 Cr EBITDA). Third, capex diluted asset turns in the near term. FY26's ₹60.5 Cr capex raised Net PPE to ₹112 Cr by September 2026 (from ₹64 Cr in March 2026), pulling net fixed asset turnover down from 3.1x to 2.8x. On the bright side, debt is near zero (D/E 0.01x, ₹5.7 Cr short-term debt vs. ₹488 Cr net worth on Sep 30, 2026). In addition, ₹8 Cr of bank credit lines sat completely unused.

Ten-Year Balance-Sheet Quality & Liquidity Buffer (FY15–H1 FY27): Across a decade of mining swings, balance-sheet caution has been Eimco Elecon's hallmark. Net worth grew steadily from retained profits to ₹488 Cr as of September 30, 2026. Against that equity, the company held just ₹5.7 Cr of short-term borrowings (D/E 0.01x) and ₹8 Cr of unused bank working-capital limits. In August 2026, CRISIL reaffirmed its Crisil A/Stable and Crisil A1 ratings. CRISIL highlighted ~₹206 Cr of liquid mutual funds and treasury holdings, down slightly from ₹228 Cr in May 2025. That small dip occurred only because Eimco self-funded ₹60.5 Cr of FY26 capex without debt. Interest coverage reached 50.51x in FY26, leaving zero solvency risk even in a deep tender freeze.

Capital Turnover, Working-Capital Drag & The ROE Ceiling: Forensic accounting separates solvency from capital efficiency. Roughly 40–45% of Eimco Elecon's equity sits in single-digit-yield treasury funds. Meanwhile, operations tie up 211 days of inventory and 115 days of receivables, creating a 219-day TTM working-capital cycle. As a result, Return on Equity stayed modest at 8.6% in FY26 (9.0% TTM in H1 FY27), with ROCE at 7.5% in FY26 (11.7% TTM). The ₹60.5 Cr FY26 capex lift to ₹112 Cr of Net PPE also pulled net fixed asset turnover down from 3.1x to 2.8x. For core operating ROCE to clear 15–18%, sales must top ₹320–350 Cr on this larger asset base while inventory and debtor days fall structurally.

Ten-Year Cash & Margin Forensic Summary (FY15–FY26): Looking across the full 12-year span explains both Eimco Elecon's downturn resilience and its return ceiling. From FY15 to FY22, sales fell from ₹196 Cr to ₹84 Cr. Even so, the company never posted a full-year net loss and kept over ₹200 Cr in liquid reserves. Since FY23, operating profit jumped sharply (₹39.9 Cr in FY24, ₹56.2 Cr in FY25, ₹43.0 Cr in FY26). Yet cash conversion stays at ~51–63% of EBITDA, and Other Income (₹17.05 Cr in FY26) still drives a third of pre-tax profit. Until working-capital days shrink from 219+ days and excess cash earns higher operating returns or goes back to owners, ROE will likely stay capped near 9–13%.

web_blocks.title: Forensic Verdict on Return on Equity (ROE)
paragraphs: A debt-free maker with 18.6% EBITDA margins should normally earn 18–22% ROE. Eimco Elecon earns just 8.6–12.0% ROE because 40–45% of its balance sheet sits in low-yield treasury funds (~₹180–206 Cr). At the same time, operations tie up 211-day inventories and 115-day receivables.
Unless sales pass ₹320–350 Cr on the expanded asset base without matching working-capital bloat, ROE will stay stuck in the low double digits.

book_paragraphs: When you and I open Eimco Elecon's ten-year financial ledger, the first thing that jumps off the page is how extraordinarily safe the balance sheet looks—and the second is how slowly cash actually turns around inside the business. Over the past decade, Eimco Elecon has carried virtually zero debt, ending September 2026 with ₹488 crore of shareholders' equity against just ₹5.7 crore of short-term borrowings, while keeping its ₹8 crore of fund-based bank limits completely unutilized. That fortress conservatism earned a reaffirmed Crisil A/Stable and Crisil A1 credit rating in August 2026, backed by a 50.51x interest coverage ratio.

Yet safety is not the same thing as capital efficiency. In FY2026, Eimco Elecon earned a solid 18.6% EBITDA margin and ₹38.71 crore in net profit, yet its Return on Equity was just 8.6%—and its Return on Capital Employed was 7.5%—down from 12.0% ROE in FY25. Why does an 18.6%-margin, debt-free manufacturer earn single-digit returns on equity? Because roughly ₹206 crore of its net worth sits in mutual-fund and treasury investments earning modest single-digit yields, while the operating business ties up 211 days of inventory and 115 days of receivables, pushing the working-capital cycle above 219 days.

Look closely at the quality of earnings too. Between FY17 and FY26, non-operating Other Income regularly accounted for 25% to 45% of Profit Before Tax. In FY2026, ₹17.05 crore of Eimco Elecon's ₹50.36 crore Profit Before Tax—roughly one-third—came from treasury Other Income rather than selling underground loaders or piling rigs. When Other Income dipped in Q2 FY27, net profit margin fell by 230 basis points even though core operating EBITDA margin actually expanded by 340 basis points.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Ten-Year Cash Conversion & Capex Pivot
paragraphs: Across the ten years from FY15 to FY24, Eimco Elecon converted roughly 63% of its cumulative operating profit (₹196 crore) into operating cash flow (₹124 crore), with wild year-to-year swings—from +₹43 crore of operating cash flow in FY16 to minus ₹10 crore in FY22, +₹33.3 crore in FY25, and ₹22.1 crore in FY26. In H1 FY27, even as revenue surged 33.3% year-on-year to ₹134.3 crore, operating cash flow was just ₹2 crore because ₹16 crore was absorbed into inventories and receivables.

Meanwhile, management just completed its heaviest capital-expenditure burst in a decade—spending ₹60.5 crore in FY26, including the Kanjari land acquisition and plant expansion—lifting net fixed assets to ₹112 crore by September 2026, up from ₹64 crore in March 2026. That temporarily pulled net fixed asset turnover down from 3.1x to 2.8x, and pushed FY26 Free Cash Flow to minus ₹38.4 crore. CRISIL expects capex to revert to routine maintenance levels from FY27 onward. So the forensic test for you and me over the next two years is crystal clear: as the ₹133 crore order book converts into deliveries, does that new ₹112 crore plant generate ₹320+ crore of revenue and pull working-capital days down, or does growth keep getting trapped in the warehouse and receivables ledger?

book_subsections.title: Why a Debt-Free Fortress Still Earns Single-Digit ROE
paragraphs: Beginner investors often assume that a debt-free company with 18.6% operating margins must automatically earn a 20% Return on Equity. Eimco Elecon is a textbook case study in why that assumption fails—and why you and I always have to decompose Return on Equity into operating return and balance-sheet structure.

Look at the ₹488 crore of net worth sitting on Eimco Elecon's balance sheet as of September 2026. Roughly ₹206 crore of that equity—more than 40%—is not invested in steel lathes, R&D labs, or spare-parts depots at all. It is parked in mutual funds and liquid treasury investments earning single-digit annual yields. That ₹206 crore cash cushion is a wonderful insurance policy during a seven-year coal winter, and it keeps CRISIL comfortable reaffirming an A/Stable credit rating, but it mathematically drags down overall Return on Equity.

Now look at the remaining ~₹282 crore invested in the operating factory and working capital. Because the business carries 211 days of inventory and 115 days of receivables—and just added ₹60.5 crore of fixed assets at Kanjari and Vallabh Vidyanagar—capital turns over slowly. In FY26, net fixed asset turnover dipped from 3.1x to 2.8x, and ROE landed at 8.6%. For Eimco Elecon to graduate from a safe, cyclical engineering survivor into a genuine high-ROCE compounder, two things must happen together: revenue on the new ₹112 crore plant base must scale past ₹320 to ₹350 crore, and working-capital days must come down from 219 days toward 150 days.

book_subsections.title: The Forensic Checklist: Cash Flow vs. Accounting Profit Over a Full Cycle
paragraphs: Let us close our financial forensics with a simple mental exercise that every serious investor should run on cyclical machinery makers. Take Eimco Elecon's cumulative operating profit over the ten-year period from FY15 to FY24—₹196 crore—and compare it against cumulative Cash Flow from Operations of ₹124 crore. That 63% cash-conversion ratio tells you the unvarnished truth about the business model: over a full cycle, roughly one-third of accounting operating profit stays absorbed inside working capital to support higher inventories and receivables.

Now add the recent capital-expenditure wave to that equation. In FY26, Eimco Elecon spent ₹60.5 crore—more than its entire FY24 and FY25 capex combined ten times over—to acquire land at Kanjari and modernize manufacturing capacity. That pushed Free Cash Flow to minus ₹38.4 crore in FY26. Because CRISIL expects capex to step down to routine maintenance levels from FY27 onward, the next two years offer a clean natural experiment: if revenue scales above ₹300 to ₹350 crore on the ₹112 crore net fixed-asset base while capex normalizes, Free Cash Flow should swing sharply positive and lift core operating ROCE out of its single-digit rut.

Before we close the financial ledger, remember one practical rule about reading Eimco Elecon’s quarterly P&L: always separate core EBIT from treasury Other Income. In FY26, Other Income of ₹17.05 crore accounted for 33.9% of Profit Before Tax, softening the blow of a 6.4% revenue dip. In Q2 FY27, the reverse happened—core EBITDA margin jumped 340 basis points, yet net profit margin dipped 230 basis points simply because treasury Other Income normalized. If you judge Eimco Elecon on core operating profit and cash conversion rather than headline net profit alone, you will never be fooled by treasury timing.

Ultimately, Eimco Elecon’s balance sheet gives management the rarest luxury in Indian heavy engineering: time. With ₹206 crore in liquid reserves and virtually zero debt, the company can afford to be selective on credit terms—provided it converts that patience into higher asset turnover.

Watching how management balances that ₹206 crore liquidity cushion against Kanjari plant utilization and working-capital velocity will tell you everything you need to know about Eimco Elecon’s next five years of capital compounding.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Separating Treasury Yield from Engineering Skill
book_callouts.text: Always strip out Other Income when judging Eimco Elecon's core profitability. A company that earns ₹17 crore from mutual funds and ₹34 crore from core operations is part-industrial, part-treasury—and its operating return on capital depends entirely on turning inventory and receivables faster.
